clue.text: Misleading details in plans covering promise of redemption

indicators.note: covering means the first piece wraps around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: specs, short for specifications, are the details set out in plans
an IOU is a written promise to repay, that is to redeem a debt

explanation.surface: Somebody's plans contain deceptive small print hiding a religious-sounding pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redemption' sounds spiritual, but here it is the settling of a debt, which a signed note of hand promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an argument that is plausible on the surface but actually deceptive is so described.

clue.text: Doubly supporting mother, as a matter of politeness

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting; 'doubly' asks for two such words
for is the second word meaning in favour of, supporting
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone backs their mother twice over, purely out of good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubly supporting' asks for two different words meaning in favour of, set side by side, before the informal mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase for something done as a formality, for the sake of courtesy or convention.

clue.text: Tiger crashes disastrously — this reveals mounting cost

indicators.note: disastrously suggests things going badly wrong, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer called Tiger has a terrible car accident and the bill keeps climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrously' rearranges the letters of TIGER CRASHES. The definition is a till, whose display shows the total rising as items are rung up.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a shop till displays the running total as each purchase is added.

clue.text: Having a few degrees, and intelligent? Not so, not so!

definitions.text: Having a few degrees, and intelligent? Not so, not so!

parts.words: Having a few degrees, and intelligent? Not so, not so!
parts.note: two descriptions each denied in turn: an angle of this kind has many degrees, more than ninety, and a person of this kind is slow-witted

explanation.surface: A much-qualified graduate turns out to be neither qualified nor bright.
explanation.walkthrough: The degrees are those of an angle, not a university. Each 'not so' denies one description: not small in degrees, and not intelligent.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes both an angle wider than a right angle and a slow-witted person, the opposites of the two descriptions.

clue.text: Avoid spending money in bar

definitions.meaning: to put cash aside rather than part with it
as a preposition, bar means except or apart from

explanation.surface: A drinker tries to keep their wallet shut at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A word that means both to economise and, as a preposition, except.

clue.text: Toy with coaches in school tennis games

parts.note: as a verb, to school someone is to train them
a set is a group of games in a tennis match

explanation.surface: Somebody fiddles with the buses during school tennis matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy' reads as a verb but is a noun: a plaything that has railway coaches. 'School' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a model railway is a plaything made up of an engine, carriages and track.

clue.text: It's a north-facing area for vineyards

indicators.note: in a down entry, north-facing letters run up the grid, so they are read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A slope that faces north is being described as wine-growing land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north-facing' works only in a down clue: the letters of IT'S A are written upwards, giving the wine town in Piedmont, Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a town and district of north-west Italy famous for its sparkling wine.

clue.text: Broadcast airing after six in original state

indicators.note: after tells you the jumbled piece follows the numeral in the answer

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: broadcast can mean scattered, as seed is, so the letters next to it are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A programme goes out after six o'clock in its untouched form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like a television term but means scattered. The state is one of the thirteen original American colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the thirteen colonies that became the first states of the USA.

clue.text: King and I joining a publisher in social activity

indicators.note: joining tells you the king and I are attached to the end of the other pieces

parts.note: a press is a publishing house, as in a university press
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: The stars of a famous musical team up with a publishing house for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' attaches K and I to the end of A PRESS. 'King and I' recalls the musical but is just two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the drinking and socialising that follows a day on the slopes.

clue.text: Pitch a decisive factor in cricket match

definitions.meaning: to pitch something is to throw or fling it

definitions.text: a decisive factor in cricket match
definitions.meaning: the coin flipped before play decides which captain chooses to bat or bowl first, often shaping the result

explanation.surface: The state of the playing surface settles a game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like the cricket strip but is a verb meaning throw. Before a cricket match the captains flip a coin to decide who bats first.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both to throw and the coin flip that starts a game of cricket.

clue.text: Politicians at work maintaining domestic security

parts.note: the House is the body of members of a parliament, such as the House of Commons
a parliament is said to be sitting when it is in session and doing business

explanation.surface: Ministers are busy keeping the nation safe at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic security' sounds like national policy but means looking after someone's home while they are away.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: living in and guarding an absent owner's home.

clue.text: Trailblazers run inside to look after dogs

indicators.note: inside places the run within the word meaning to look after

parts.note: to tend something is to look after it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
setters are a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: Pioneers dash indoors to take care of their hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: people who start a fashion that others follow are pioneers.

clue.text: English writer, going by railway, leaves

indicators.note: going by puts the writer next to, and ahead of, the railway

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist

explanation.surface: An author from England departs on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' reads as a verb, departs, but it is a noun: foliage. 'going by' sets the novelist beside the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: foliage, the green growth of plants.

clue.text: Person I'm addressing, with most of the next generation

parts.note: you is the word for the person being spoken to

indicators.note: most of means the following word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A speaker talks to one person along with the bulk of the young.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun for young people, those who come after the present adults.

clue.text: Editor put in report, back in European country

indicators.note: put in says the editor is placed within the other piece
back, coming straight after report, means that word is read from its end

parts.note: news is a report of recent events

explanation.surface: A journalist's article goes in, with its editor's name added, back on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Scandinavian nation and member of the EU.

clue.text: Land in Africa, part of Somalia

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a stretch of letters within the following word

explanation.surface: An aircraft touches down in a region of an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' reads as a verb but is a noun, a country. 'part of' takes four consecutive letters from SOMALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a landlocked West African republic.

clue.text: One needed in dreadful endemic?

indicators.note: needed in says the one must be placed within the letters that follow
dreadful suggests something in a bad state, so the letters of the next word are disordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A terrible outbreak of disease calls for a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges ENDEMIC into MEDCINE and 'needed in' puts I inside. The whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a remedy or drug is what a population wants when disease is rife.

clue.text: Where things may be stored underground for spring

definitions.text: Where things may be stored underground
definitions.meaning: a secure cellar or strongroom below ground, as in a bank
as a verb, to spring is to leap over something

explanation.surface: Supplies are laid down in a cellar ready for the warmer season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both a strongroom or cellar and to leap over something.

clue.text: Saintly female I see speaking in Italian city

indicators.note: in places the spoken letters within the name of the city

parts.note: Verona is a city in northern Italy

indicators.note: speaking says the two words before it are heard, not read, giving two letter names

parts.note: said aloud, I see is heard as the letter names I and C

explanation.surface: A holy woman says she understands while in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' turns 'I see' into the letters I C, and 'in' puts them inside VERONA. St Veronica wiped Christ's face on the way to Calvary.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the name of a woman venerated as a saint in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Facts that can be twisted a little

indicators.note: that can be twisted says the phrase after it may be turned round end to end

parts.note: a tad is an informal phrase for a little

explanation.surface: Somebody admits that the truth can be bent slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that can be twisted' turns A TAD round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pieces of information, figures or statistics.

clue.text: Paintings put up with some biblical text and cross

indicators.note: put up, in a down entry, means the word before it is written upwards

parts.note: paintings are a form of art
a verse is a numbered short section of a chapter of the Bible

explanation.surface: Religious pictures are hung on a wall together with scripture and a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ART into TRA. 'cross' is a verb here, to go across.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to travel or pass over something from one side to the other.

clue.text: Stop protecting one who's happy to be a loser?

definitions.text: who's happy to be a loser?

indicators.note: protecting means the first word shelters the next piece within itself

parts.note: to deter someone is to stop or discourage them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Somebody is told to quit shielding a person content to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts I inside DETER. The loser is someone glad to lose weight, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a person cutting down on food is pleased when the scales show less weight.

clue.text: Assistant in theatre, perhaps, announced poet

indicators.note: announced says the poet's name is heard rather than read

parts.note: A E Housman was the English poet who wrote A Shropshire Lad

explanation.surface: A stagehand at the playhouse is introduced as a writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' makes it the sound of the poet's surname. The theatre is an operating theatre: in British hospitals this is a junior resident doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a junior hospital doctor in Britain, who may help surgeons during operations.

clue.text: Harmony seldom initially found in marriage

indicators.note: found in says the single letter sits within the word for marriage

parts.note: a marriage is a union of two people

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that wedded couples rarely get along at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S from SELDOM and 'found in' places it inside UNION.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: complete agreement, or voices sounding together at one pitch.

clue.text: Recital isn't arranged ahead of time for musician

indicators.note: ahead of puts the jumbled letters before the abbreviation that follows
arranged means the letters of the two words before it are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A performer's concert has not been set up early enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe counts for nothing: only the letters of the two opening words are used, and the surface's concert is just raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a player of a woodwind instrument.

clue.text: A river journey in old vessel

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
to journey is to go

explanation.surface: Someone takes a trip downstream in an ancient boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The vessel is Jason's ship in Greek myth, in which the Argonauts sought the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the ship of Jason in Greek legend.

clue.text: Gratuitous advice?

parts.note: gratuitous is stretched to mean having to do with gratuities, the money left for a waiter, a word that also means helpful hints

explanation.definitionFit: Pun: the word for sums left for waiters also means useful hints or pointers.

clue.text: Monarch that's rejected in this republic

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters before it are read from the end

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth II
IE, short for id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A nation has thrown out its king or queen and become a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the Irish-language name for Ireland, which has a president and no monarch, so the surface is true of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Irish-language name for Ireland, a state with a president rather than a crown.

clue.text: Patching damaged headgear that's not worn out

indicators.note: damaged means the word before it is broken up and its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Someone mends a battered hat that still has some life in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges PATCHING. 'not worn out' means not worn outdoors: this is a hat for bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a soft hat once put on for sleeping, so never seen outdoors.

clue.text: Menacing relative outside home

indicators.note: outside means the relative goes around the word for home

parts.note: a sister is a family relative
in means at home

explanation.surface: A threatening family member lurks in front of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: threatening, suggesting evil or harm to come.
